title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1RC0RF_0LD---_1LE1LD_1RA0LB_0RE0RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Same mechanism as 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD---: a 110101010 bouncer on the left, and on the slow right a sorted list of blocks 1^(6j+1) 00 (37, 41, 43, 47, 49, 53, …) rewritten by passing waves; open.
Lean proves no halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps (the first 10,000 by the kernel alone), 8 shift rules of the sweeps; the rest of the description below is observation of the run, marked as such.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 32,838 cells have been visited and 25,123 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.15).

claims.title: 8 shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: For every n and every tape around: A crosses 110101010 rightward writing 001111111, D crosses it leftward writing 111011101 (eight proved rules over its rotations). Each is a theorem steps (s·n) … = some … found and proved by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (C reading 1) needs 11100 or 11111 to the left; any right side starting with 1. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.title: Macro structure: bouncer with a sorted list of blocks 1^(6j+1)
claims.text: Left of the start: (110 10 10 10) repeated, a √t bouncer (proved shift rules). Right of it, on the slow side (394 cells after 109 steps), a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00 whose settled lengths are 6j + 1, sorted, with 6j + 5 blocks at group boundaries, e.g. at step 945,073,674: 41 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 7 : 1 : 47 : 49 : 49 : 11 : 1 : 53 : 55 : 59 : 5 : 1 : 1 : 3 : 1 (run lengths, : = 00).

claims.title: 8 shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: For every n and every tape around: A crosses 110101010 rightward writing 001111111, D crosses it leftward writing 111011101 (eight proved rules over its rotations). Each is a theorem steps (s·n) … = some … found and proved by tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py.

claims.title: Where a halt can happen (closed tape language, 5-cell windows)
claims.text: The closure search of bbtools.ctl with windows of 5 cells is closed but allows halts; the halting abstract configurations constrain the neighbourhood of a halt: a halt (C reading 1) needs 11100 or 11111 to the left; any right side starting with 1. A Python check, not a Lean certificate (the Lean library only has the right-edge and no-halt corollaries, which do not apply).

claims.text: Left of the start: (110 10 10 10) repeated, a √t bouncer (proved shift rules). Right of it, on the slow side (394 cells after 109 steps), a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00 whose settled lengths are 6j + 1, sorted, with 6j + 5 blocks at group boundaries, e.g. at step 945,073,674: 41 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 7 : 1 : 47 : 49 : 49 : 11 : 1 : 53 : 55 : 59 : 5 : 1 : 1 : 3 : 1 (run lengths, : = 00).

claims.title: No halt in the first 8.29×10<sup>13</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 8.29×1013 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.01×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 7,944 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. C reading 1 halts. The 5-cell closed language allows that with 11100/11111 on the left and any right window starting with 1.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA0RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 2 other holdouts (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 32,838 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

facts.text: No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.01×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: What the machine does: bouncer with a sorted list of blocks 1^(6j+1)
html: Left of the start: (110 10 10 10) repeated, a √t bouncer (proved shift rules). Right of it, on the slow side (394 cells after 109 steps), a list of blocks of 1s separated by 00 whose settled lengths are 6j + 1, sorted, with 6j + 5 blocks at group boundaries, e.g. at step 945,073,674: 41 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 43 : 7 : 1 : 47 : 49 : 49 : 11 : 1 : 53 : 55 : 59 : 5 : 1 : 1 : 3 : 1 (run lengths, : = 00).

The first records coincide with those of 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD--- (same block lists, different step counts: the two machines share the mechanism with different costs per pass); after a while the two runs diverge but keep the same structure.

sections.heading: What a halt would require
html: C reading 1 halts. The 5-cell closed language allows that with 11100/11111 on the left and any right window starting with 1.

sections.heading: What is proved, and what is not
html:
• Sweeps (lean/Sweeps.lean, kernel): A crosses 110101010 rightward writing 001111111, D crosses it leftward writing 111011101 (eight proved rules over its rotations); for every number of copies and every tape around.
  • Bounded run (lean/Blank.lean): no halt in 107 steps (native), 10,000 (kernel); the halting transition is the only way to stop.
Everything else on this page is observation of the simulated run (heuristic). Nothing here decides halting.

sections.heading: What would move it forward
html: As for the twin: the rule of one wall visit on the block list.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.15).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,838 cells (23,688 left of the start, 394 right), with a density of 1s of 0.765.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB1RA_1LC0RD_1LD1LB_1LE0LF_0RA---_0LB0LF: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA0RF: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→A, F→F; it is this table started in state E

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0RD---: 8,004,077 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 8,004,076 there
  • 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LE_1LC0RF_0RD---: 8,004,077 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 8,004,076 there
